text:
This looks like mid-2008. Fed funds are at 2.09%, which fits the period after the cuts through April 2008 (2.00%). Headline CPI is 4.12%, consistent with May 2008 (4.2%) or June 2008 (5.0%). The Baa-Treasury spread of 3.47 fits too.

Checking against the data: the 10-year yield of 3.47% is low for June 2008, when it was about 4.0%. In March 2008 it was around 3.4%, and the 2-year was 1.67%, which also matches March 2008 (about 1.6%). Fed funds averaged 2.61% in March and 2.28% in April, and 2.09% is roughly the May 2008 average, while the March average of 2.61% would be too high.

Other cues:
- Payrolls were negative on a 3-month average, which fits early 2008.
- The VIX at 25.7 fits March 2008 (about 25–30).
- Equity returns over 3 months of -10.2% fit end of March 2008, since the S&P was down about 9.9% in Q1.
- Gold was down 5.8% in the month, consistent with a March 2008 pullback from its peak near $1000.
- Emerging-market equity was down 7.6% in the month, which also fits March 2008.
- Headline CPI of 4.12% matches March 2008 (4.0%).
- The 12-month change in fed funds of -3.21 implies about 5.3% a year earlier, which fits March 2007 and so supports March 2008.

For fed funds, the effective rate in March 2008 was about 2.2% at month end, since the cut to 2.25% came on March 18, so 2.09% is plausible.

The 12-month dollar change of -9.35% is also consistent with March 2008.
